battle.name: 913-927年拜占庭-保加利亞戰爭
battle.theater: 君士坦丁堡與色雷斯海岸線
battle.brief: 913年夏，保加利亞沙皇西梅翁一世大軍西進，兵臨君士坦丁堡，圍城延續一年；拜占庭其後遠征，卻於920年8月20日在阿凱勞斯河畔被西梅翁與佩切涅格騎兵擊潰，主帥利奧·福卡斯被俘。圍城期間守軍以連發弩等速射火器把攻城隊形壓在牆外，卡面秦連弩正是這種可重複上弦、單兵可操的守城利器。

kit.name: 秦連弩
kit.history: 弩機把拉力存起來，一踩一發。守城的一方靠它把攻城的人壓在牆外。

countries: 這場戰爭正式稱為913至927年的拜占庭—保加利亞戰爭，但留下完整戰事記錄的只有拜占庭一方的編年史：《Theophanes Continuatus》，即《狄奧菲內斯認罪者編年史》的匿名續篇，以及十二世紀約翰·斯基利茲的《歷史概論》。拜占庭方面，交戰主體是君士坦丁堡的皇帝朝廷：913年6月皇帝亞歷山德去世，七歲的君士坦丁七世登基，攝政由佐伊·卡爾博諾普西娜與兩位宦官西奧菲亞尼斯、提奧克提斯托斯共同掌握，軍國大事須與軍需大臣（logothete tou drome）協商。軍隊方面有首都禁衛軍（tagmata）、小亞細亞與愛琴海各軍區的部隊、色雷斯的省軍，以及由海軍元帥（droungarios tou ploimou）率領的艦隊；攻城器械與軍械庫歸工程總監（epistrategos tou strategeou）管轄，狄奧多西城牆由城防軍（ophylakes）與守城民兵駐守。教會方面，自916年起主持教務的宗主教尼古勞斯·彌斯提科斯組織遊行祝禱，被編年史視為士氣與正統的支柱。保加利亞方面，主力是沙皇西梅翁一世統率的保加利亞軍，以保加爾人為核心並吸收斯拉夫等部族兵力的混合軍隊，國都普雷斯拉夫，兵源來自色雷斯、馬其頓與多瑙河下游的邊軍；西梅翁還把佩切涅格人收編為盟友與僱傭騎兵。外交上，拜占庭同時拉攏匈牙利人、威尼斯人與東方阿拔斯王朝，希望在多線制衡保加利亞。雙方留下的正式和約文本無從查考，如今可以確認的只是那份三十年和約的效力，以及其後的多次撕毀。
countriesEn: The conflict is formally known as the Byzantine-Bulgarian War of 913-927, but the only continuous account of it comes from the Byzantine side: the anonymous continuation of the Chronicle of Theophanes the Confessor, known as the Theophanes Continuatus, and the twelfth-century Synopsis Historion of John Skylitzes. On the Byzantine side the belligerent was the imperial court at Constantinople. Emperor Alexander died in June 913 and the seven-year-old Constantine VII Porphyrogenitus succeeded him, with the regency shared between Zoe Karbonopsina and the eunuchs Theophanes and Theoktistos, who decided military affairs in consultation with the logothete tou drome. The armed forces comprised the capital tagmata, the field armies of the Anatolian and Aegean themes, the provincial troops of Thrace, and a fleet under the droungarios tou ploimou; siege engines and the armoury were the responsibility of the epistrategos tou strategeou, while the Theodosian walls of Constantinople were manned by the ophylakes and the civic guard. On the church side, the Patriarch Nicholas Mystikos, in office from 916, organised the processions and the blessings, and the chroniclers treat him as a pillar of morale and of legitimacy. On the Bulgarian side the main force was the army of Tsar Simeon I, a mixed host built around the Bulgars and drawing in Slav and other tribal contingents, mustered from the Thracian, Macedonian and Lower-Danubian frontier districts, with the capital at Preslav. Simeon also enrolled the Pechenegs as allies and as hired cavalry. Diplomatically, Byzantium simultaneously courted the Magyars, the Venetians and the Abbasid caliphate, hoping to balance Bulgaria on several fronts at once. No formal treaty text survives from either side; what can be confirmed today is the effect of that thirty-year peace and of its later violations.
people: 西梅翁一世（約864—927），本名辛美（Shumiy），是 Boris I 的次子，893年其父退位後以保加利亞執政者的名號起家，913年圍城時已自稱皇帝。他用兵講求工程與速度，先後圍攻塞爾迪卡與普雷斯拉夫，並在普雷斯拉夫建起帶希臘式宮殿與書院、可與君士坦丁堡抗衡的另一座帝國中心，延攬君士坦丁堡的文人；但史料對他性格有兩種描寫，有的說他用兵果決善於攻城，有的說他急於稱帝而屢失戰機。拜占庭方面的關鍵人物是海軍元帥利奧·福卡斯（老福卡斯）：他參與917與919年的遠征，又在920年8月20日阿凱勞斯河畔被俘，獲釋後帶回西梅翁的和平信。他的搭檔巴達斯（福卡斯的姻親）曾在919年與他分兵深入色雷斯，遠征瓦解後兩人同受貶抑。君士坦丁七世只是名義上的統帥，真正裁決的是攝政方，編年史把920年的敗績部分歸咎於宦官西奧菲亞尼斯的干預。宗主教尼古勞斯·彌斯提科斯在遠征前率領手持引路者聖像的遊行隊伍祝禱出征，921年圍城期間他再次主持守城的祈禱儀式。留下記載的《Theophanes Continuatus》作者與約翰·斯基利茲都是事後的編纂者，並未親臨戰場，人物細節因此帶有明顯的轉述色彩。
peopleEn: Simeon I (c. 864-927), born Shumiy, was the second son of Boris I. When his father withdrew from the throne in 893 he began to rule as archon of the Bulgars, and by the siege of 913 he already bore the title of emperor. He campaigned with a taste for engineering and speed, besieging Serdica and then Preslav, and he built at Preslav an imperial centre of his own with Greek-style palaces and a school of books, luring scholars away from Constantinople. The sources give two portraits of his character: some call him decisive and skilled at sieges, others accuse him of hurrying after the imperial title and of missing his chances. The decisive Byzantine figure was the droungarios tou ploimou Leo Phokas the Elder, who served in the expeditions of 917 and 919 and was taken prisoner at the river Achelous on 20 August 920; on his release he carried Simeon's peace letter back to Constantinople. His partner Bardas, who was linked to Phokas by marriage, marched with him into Thrace in 919, and both were disgraced when that expedition collapsed. Constantine VII was commander in name only; the regency actually decided matters, and the chroniclers lay part of the blame for 920 on the interference of the eunuch Theophanes. Patriarch Nicholas Mystikos led a procession with the Hodegetria icon to bless the army before the expeditions, and he again organised the defensive prayers of the siege in 921. The author of the Theophanes Continuatus and John Skylitzes were both later compilers who never saw the battlefield, so the personal details they preserve are visibly at second hand.
kits: 卡面這件秦連弩是漢代以降中國的技術：弩機把拉力儲存起來，踩下踏桿或轉動絞盤即可重新上弦，矢匣一次可裝數十支小弩矢，單兵即可操持，不需要像羅馬式大弩或拜占庭的繃簧弩那樣靠多人搬運。它在歐亞大陸的西傳有文本痕跡：狄奧菲內斯認罪者編年史在描述七世紀波斯人進攻君士坦丁堡時，提到一種名為χόννη的武器，學界多認為那正是中國連弩或其西傳衍生型；到了十世紀，可重複上弦的速射弩在拜占庭的器械體系中已不屬罕見，只是編年史不為它們逐一命名。就這場戰爭而言，913與921年兩次圍城都需要在城頭長時間維持密集而廉價的火力，把攻城的密集隊形壓在牆外，連發弩單兵可攜、再上弦迅捷的特性正好補在守城射擊陣位上，可置於城牆步道、塔樓與城門頂，與守城主力武器互補。同期拜占庭守城方已知的配備包括手拉一發的弩（cheiroballistra，即利奧六世戰術所載的單臂與四臂繃簧弩，統稱tetrapendylon）、手投火罐（cheiriphon）、希臘火（見於七、八世紀圍城記錄，此役是否使用不見明文），以及配置在海門與船上的投火裝置。保加利亞與佩切涅格騎兵則是典型的草原弓騎兵，配複合反曲弓、短彎刀、標槍與圓盾，靠騎射與衝鋒製造壓力；攻城端另有雲梯、攻城塔與撞錘，但編年史對這些器械的記載相當簡略。
kitsEn: The card shows the Chinese repeating crossbow, a technology of the Han era and later: the trigger mechanism stores the draw, the string is re-cocked by stepping on a pedal or turning a winch, and the magazine holds several dozen light bolts, so a single man can work the weapon without the crews needed to move a Roman-style great bolt or a Byzantine torsion ballista. Its spread westward across Eurasia left a trace in the texts: in the Chronicle of Theophanes the Confessor, describing the Persian assault on Constantinople in the seventh century, a weapon called chonnē is mentioned, and most scholars identify it with the Chinese repeating crossbow or a western derivative of it. By the tenth century, crossbows capable of being re-cocked quickly were no rarities in the Byzantine arsenal of engines, even though the chroniclers do not name them one by one. For this war in particular, the sieges of 913 and 921 both demanded dense and cheap fire from the parapets, holding the massed formations of the besiegers against the wall; the single-man portability and the speed of re-cocking of the repeating crossbow fitted exactly into the defensive firing positions, on the wall walk, in the towers and above the gates, complementing the heavier wall weapons. The documented Byzantine defensive equipment of the same period included the single-shot bolt weapons cheiroballistra, that is, the one-armed and four-armed torsion ballistae described in Leo VI's Tactica and collectively called tetrapendylon, the hand-thrown fire-pots cheeriphon, Greek fire attested in the sieges of the seventh and eighth centuries though no explicit mention for this war survives, and the fire-throwing devices mounted on the sea gates and on ships. The Bulgarian and Pecheneg horsemen were typical steppe bow riders, armed with composite recurved bows, short sabres, javelins and round shields, applying pressure through mounted archery and charges; on the attacking side they had ladders, siege towers and rams, but the chroniclers describe such engines only very briefly.
tactics: 913年的圍城是一場雙向封鎖：保加利亞軍在色雷斯平原展開，陸路壓住通往首都的大道，海上以船隊封鎖金角灣與博斯普魯斯海峽的航路，切斷君士坦丁堡的糧食與援兵；拜占庭守軍則靠狄奧多西城牆的分段塔樓、封鎖海門的鐵鏈與出海的巡邏艦隊維持補給線，多次以夜襲與小型突擊消耗城外營壘，與此同時宗主教主持的祝禱遊行被編年史當作士氣的來源。919年的反攻是拜占庭唯一一次主動出擊：兩支縱隊在色雷斯分道，試圖直取普雷斯拉夫，並以艦隊沿黑海海岸掩護陸軍北翼，但補給線拉得過長、地方守軍抵抗與缺糧令遠征在沒有交戰的情況下便告瓦解，軍心隨之崩落。920年8月20日阿凱勞斯河畔的戰鬥最能說明雙方差異：拜占庭軍沿海岸大道推進，縱隊拉長、側翼暴露，西梅翁以保加爾步兵正面牽制、佩切涅格騎兵迂迴包抄斷其退路，利奧·福卡斯所乘的馬在亂軍中中箭，他本人被俘，成建制的拜占庭軍在縱隊斷裂下崩散。921年西梅翁再度返回首都城下，這次圍城因季節、攻城器械不足與守軍抵抗而未能成功，軍隊最終撤回保加利亞。整體而言，圍城方靠騎兵機動與游擊取勝，守城方靠城牆與速射火器固守，而這正是連發弩最能發揮作用的環境。
tacticsEn: The siege of 913 was a blockade in both directions. The Bulgarian host deployed across the Thracian plain, closed the roads to the capital on the land side and sealed the routes through the Golden Horn and the Bosphorus with its ships, cutting grain and reinforcements from Constantinople. The defenders relied on the segmented towers of the Theodosian walls, on the chain across the sea gates and on cruising squadrons to keep the supply route open; they wore down the camps outside by night raids and small sorties, while the processions and blessings led by the patriarch were recorded as the source of morale. The counter-offensive of 919 was Byzantium's only active attempt: two columns divided in Thrace tried to strike at Preslav while the fleet covered the northern flank along the Black Sea coast, but the supply line was stretched too far and resistance by the local garrisons and a lack of provisions broke the expedition apart without a battle, and the army's nerve went with it. The engagement of 20 August 920 at the river Achelous shows the difference between the two sides most clearly. The Byzantine army advanced along the coastal road with its column stretched out and its flanks exposed; Simeon held the Byzantine front with Bulgar infantry while the Pecheneg cavalry wheeled round and cut the retreat; the horse of Leo Phokas was struck down in the melee, Phokas himself was taken, and the coherent Byzantine force dissolved as its column broke. In 921 Simeon came back under the walls once more, and that siege failed because of the season, a shortage of siege engines and the resistance of the garrison, so the army withdrew to Bulgaria. In general the besiegers won by mounted manoeuvre and raiding, the defended by their walls and by rapid-fire missile weapons, and that was exactly the environment in which the repeating crossbow did its best work.
data: 可核對的硬數字不多，但幾個節點相當確定：戰爭自913年夏起，至927年沙皇西梅翁病逝，前後十四年；其中真正的決定性交鋒集中在919至921年，920年8月20日是全戰役唯一有明確日期的野戰。地理上，首都君士坦丁堡到阿凱勞斯（今日保加利亞黑海沿岸波莫里耶一帶）沿海岸大道約二百公里，遠征軍的後勤基地因此完全依賴首都與海運；保加利亞首都普雷斯拉夫距多瑙河約三百公里，與拜占庭邊境之間夾著整個色雷斯平原。西梅翁在913年第一次圍城時投入的兵力，編年史只以數萬形容規模，其中相當一部分是附庸的邊軍與佩切涅格騎兵；920年拜占庭出戰的野戰軍同樣是數萬量級，且有大量亞美尼亞、基比里亞等軍區部隊未能及時抵達。防禦方可倚賴的城牆數字是固定的：狄奧多西城牆陸線約五點五公里、海牆約八點五公里，全線近十四公里，陸牆共有九十六座塔樓；城頭常備的守備兵力在數千量級，弓弩手的密度決定了圍城能拖多久。戰後三十年和約約定927年之後三十年間互不侵犯，該條約一直維持到954年才被西梅翁二世撕毀。
dataEn: Hard numbers that can be checked are few, but several anchors are firm. The war ran from the summer of 913 to the death of Tsar Simeon in 927, fourteen years in all; the decisive operations were concentrated in 919-921, and 20 August 920 is the only field engagement in the whole war with an exact date. Geographically, the distance from Constantinople to Achelous, on the Black Sea coast of modern Bulgaria near Pomorie, is about two hundred kilometres by the coastal road, so the base of the expedition's logistics lay entirely in the capital and its shipping; the Bulgarian capital Preslav stands some three hundred kilometres from the Danube, and the whole Thracian plain lies between it and the Byzantine frontier. For the first siege of 913 the chroniclers describe the force Simeon committed only as tens of thousands, a large part of it made up of subordinate frontier troops and Pecheneg horsemen; the Byzantine field army in 920 was of comparable order, and detachments from the Armenian and Kibyrrhaiotai themes had not arrived in time. The figures of the defences are fixed: the land wall of the Theodosian circuit measures about five and a half kilometres, the sea wall about eight and a half, the whole circuit close to fourteen kilometres, and the land wall carries ninety-six towers. The permanent garrison of the walls was in the thousands, and the density of archers and crossbowmen on the parapets decided how long a siege could be held off. The thirty-year peace agreed after the war bound the two sides to refrain from aggression for thirty years from 927; it held until 954, when Simeon II tore it up.
cause: 導火索是保加利亞在拜占庭南方邊境取得了戰略主動權。克魯姆在811年攻陷普拉卡後，拜占庭被迫承認保加利亞在多瑙河外的主權，並約定由帝國支付貢金；894年克魯姆在東方受挫後，帝國曾企圖以進攻取消這筆代價，卻在得斯波提查戰役慘敗。此後帝國長期拖延乃至欠付，直到913年才正式宣告廢除貢金安排；據編年史記載，一位保加利亞使者對拜占庭朝廷留下過一句話，要皇帝自己來取他想拿的東西。圍城之後，拜占庭轉而以外交攻勢孤立西梅翁：出錢拉攏匈牙利人與佩切涅格人從背後襲擾色雷斯，試圖在多瑙河與色雷斯之間切斷保加利亞的戰爭縱深；919年的遠征正是這條外交線的延伸，目的在於趁西梅翁攻勢受阻而重奪主動權，但敗於阿凱勞斯後，帝國只剩兩條路：接受在西梅翁所指定的條件下議和，或讓戰爭再拖一年。深層原因則是西梅翁的帝國計劃：他要在普雷斯拉夫建都、加冕為皇帝，並取得獨立教會的宗主教地位，這三件事都無法靠軍力單獨完成。
causeEn: The trigger was the fact that Bulgaria had seized the strategic initiative on Byzantium's southern frontier. After Krum took Pliska in 811, the empire was forced to recognise Bulgarian lordship beyond the Danube and to promise tribute; when Krum was checked in the east in 894, the empire tried to erase that price by invading and suffered a crushing defeat at the battle of the Deep Gates in 894. Thereafter the empire stalled and short-paid, and only in 913 did it formally declare the tribute arrangement cancelled; according to the chronicler, a Bulgarian envoy left the Byzantine court with the message that if the emperor wanted his share, he should come and take it himself. After the siege the Byzantines turned to a diplomatic offensive designed to isolate Simeon: they paid the Magyars and the Pechenegs to raid Thrace from the rear, hoping to cut the Bulgarian war effort between the Danube and Thrace. The expedition of 919 was the armed extension of that policy, launched in the hope of seizing the initiative while Simeon's offensive had stalled; after the defeat at Achelous the empire had only two choices left, to make peace on terms dictated by Simeon or to let the war drag on for another year. The deeper cause lies in Simeon's imperial programme: a capital at Preslav, a coronation as emperor and an autocephalous church with its own metropolitan were three aims that military force alone could not deliver.
impact: 這場戰爭的結果在十世紀初並未立即改變邊界，卻徹底改變了兩國的自我認知與歐亞草原的權力格局。對拜占庭而言，首都連續兩年面對城外的軍營，等於承認帝國最富庶的行省首都在十世紀時仍可能被一個內陸國家逼到城牆上死守；而拜占庭在外交上大量動用匈牙利人與佩切涅格人作為制衡工具，開啟了此後百餘年草原族群被系統性引入巴爾干的先例——這些僱傭騎兵在930年代之後陸續出現在保加利亞、匈牙利與拜占庭的戰場上，成為帝國無法擺脫的變數。對保加利亞而言，西梅翁在普雷斯拉夫建成的文學院與希臘化宮廷被後世視為第一保加利亞文學的中心，保存了大量中世紀早期東南歐的文獻；而919至921年的敗仗迫使西梅翁接受議和，等於用戰爭的失敗換來國家的長久存在期限。教會層面的影響最為深遠：西梅翁要求宗主教區的承認，927年君士坦丁堡宗主教區同意設立保加利亞大主教區，保加利亞教會取得自治地位並自行發展，成為此後君士坦丁堡與羅馬之間另一個長期爭議的源頭。
impactEn: The outcome of this war changed no frontier in the early tenth century, yet it thoroughly altered how the two empires understood themselves and how power was distributed on the Eurasian steppe. For Byzantium, two consecutive years with the enemy camp outside the capital amounted to an admission that the richest provincial capital of the empire could still be pinned against its own walls by an inland power; and the heavy use of Magyars and Pechenegs as instruments of balance set a precedent for the systematic employment of steppe peoples in the Balkans for the century that followed, those hired horsemen appearing from the 930s onward in the battlefields of Bulgaria, Hungary and Byzantium alike as a factor the empire could not shake off. For Bulgaria, the school of Preslav and the Greek-style court that Simeon built up came to be seen as the centre of the first Bulgarian literature, preserving a large body of early medieval south-eastern European texts; and the defeats of 919-921, which forced Simeon to accept a peace, exchanged a military failure for a long stretch of national existence. The deepest effect lay in the church: Simeon's demand for a metropolitan was met in 927, when the patriarchate of Constantinople agreed to the establishment of a Bulgarian archbishopric, and the Bulgarian church obtained an autocephalous status of its own and developed on its own lines, becoming the source of yet another long-running dispute between Constantinople and Rome.
result: 西梅翁的第三次選擇不是再打一場圍城，而是議和。920年8月阿凱勞斯之敗後，佩切涅格人主張殺死被俘的利奧·福卡斯，福卡斯則請求被送回君士坦丁堡，以便代皇帝談判；西梅翁放他回國並附上親筆信，直接向君士坦丁七世提出締和。921年保加利亞軍再度逼近首都卻未能攻破城防，此後雙方在924至926年間落實一紙長達三十年的和約：西梅翁保住普雷斯拉夫與其對多瑙河外實際的統治，帝國承認其實質獨立並允許保加利亞教會擁有宗主教區，君士坦丁七世朝廷則以承認一位對手皇帝換取南方邊界數十年的安寧。927年西梅翁病逝，次子弗拉基米爾在位短促，弟弟伊萬·阿森繼位，和約繼續維持；但在954年西梅翁二世撕毀和約、拜占庭出兵報復之前，帝國與保加利亞之間維持了整整數十年的和平與文化交流期。
resultEn: Simeon's third decision was not another siege but a negotiated peace. After the defeat at Achelous in August 920 the Pechenegs argued for killing the captive Leo Phokas; Phokas asked instead to be sent back to Constantinople so that he could negotiate for the emperor. Simeon let him go with a letter in his own hand, offering terms directly to Constantine VII. The Bulgarian army came up against the capital once more in 921 and failed to break the defences, and between 924 and 926 the two sides gave effect to a peace lasting thirty years: Simeon kept Preslav and his effective rule beyond the Danube, the empire acknowledged his de facto independence and allowed the Bulgarian church its metropolitan, and the court of Constantine VII bought a decade of quiet on the southern frontier by recognising a rival emperor. Simeon died in 927; his son Vladimir reigned briefly, and his brother Ivan Asen succeeded him, and the peace was kept. It was only in 954, when Simeon II tore up the treaty and Byzantium moved to punish him, that the long stretch of peace and cultural contact between the two states came to an end.
